title: Leah, 30: The 1% Fee That Could Cost $77,000

scenes.say: A 1% yearly fee could cost Leah about $77,000 over 30 years.
She's 30 and invests $400 a month. The fund charges 1% a year.
One percent sounds tiny, but it's charged on her whole balance, every year.
Say the market earned roughly 7% a year. Not guaranteed, just an example.
Over 30 years, the gap between those two keeps getting wider.
At 6%, she'd have about $402,000. At 6.9%, about $478,000.
Her fix: find the expense ratio, compare low-cost funds, and check it once a year.
Do you know your fund's fee? Subscribe, before a 1% fee and $77,000 are gone.

description: Leah, 30, invests $400 a month in a fund that charges 1% a year. If the market returned roughly 7% (not guaranteed), that fee could leave her about $77,000 behind a 0.1% fund after 30 years. Example math only with rounded US estimates — real returns vary and can be negative.
